newsitem.title: USA: CIA confirms pickup driver crashed on doorstep.
newsitem.headline: CIA confirms pickup driver crashed on doorstep.

text.p: A man in a pickup truck drove through security gates at the U.S. Central Intelligence Agency's headquarters last month and crashed onto the front steps, the agency said on Wednesday.

"It happened. We've learned from it and we're doing everything we can to prevent it from ever happening again," a CIA spokesman said of the December 23 incident, which had not previously been reported.

CIA security officers assigned to monitor traffic approaching the agency's main gate did not have enough time to activate pop-up iron barriers "due to the very high speed of the vehicle," which shot past them at about 8 p.m., spokesman Mark Mansfield said.
A U.S. official said the pickup's driver, identified as David O. Crump from McLean, Virginia -- where CIA headquarters is located -- apparently was mentally disturbed.
The CIA said Crump, who was arrested by CIA security guards at the scene, had no known terrorist connections, criminal background or affiliation with the spy agency.

Asked whether heads would roll at the agency because of the security breach, Mansfield said: "I dont have any comment on that. Rather than trying to assign blame, the focus is and should be on enhancing physical security."
